Mediales Kompartiment:
Geringe oberflächliche Knorpelirrgeularitäten femorotibial. Kein tiefgreifender oder fokaler Knorpeldefekt. Verdacht auf beginnenden basisnahen Einriss im Innenmeniskus am Übergang der Pars intermedia zum Hinterhorn mit minimalem Knochenödem am medialen Tibiaplateau. Ansonsten regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal (Serie 4/ Image 19). Intaktes MCL.

Laterales Kompartiment:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Geringe oberflächliche Knorpelirrgeularitäten femorotibial. Kein tiefgreifender oder fokaler Knorpeldefekt. Intakter Außenmeniskus. Intaktes LCL.

Femoropatellares Gleitlager und Trochlea:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Fokale oberflächliche Knorpelirregularität an der medialen Patellafacette (Serie 7/ Image 9). Kein tiefgreifender oder vollschichtiger Knorpeldefekt. Regelrechte Darstellung der Quadrizeps- und Patellarsehne. Regelrechte Darstellung des Hoffa`schen Fettkörpers.

Kreuzbänder:
Geringe mukoide Veränderungen des VKB. Keine Ruptur. Intaktes HKB.

Muskulatur und übrige Weichteile:
Mäßiger Gelenkerguss mit verdickter Synovia und synovialen Proliferationen.

In the medial compartment, there is longitudinal vertical tear at the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury.  
  
 The lateral compartment, there is vertical longitudinal tear of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus with flip into the intercondylar notch and flip directly posterior to a truncated anterior horn. There is focal high grade chondral injury (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at the posterolateral tibial plateau (about 1.7*1.7 cm).  
  
 The patellofemaoral joint appears congruent. There is no cartilage injury. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
  
 There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is stretching. There is no anterior tibial translation.  
 The medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Minimal amount of left knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. Medial synovial plica 6 mm - Lateral meniscus; vertical longitudinal tear of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus with flipped meniscus 
 - ACL; complete torn 
 - PCL; stretching  
 - Medial synovial plica 6 mm

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.16 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Bone marrow signal is normal. No acute fracture or bone bruise. 

JOINT SPACE:
Minimal joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Minimal, ruptured Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is mild cartilage fissuring at the central aspect of the medial femoral condyle near the intercondylar notch, with evidence of underlying healed osteochondral lesion.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Intact. However, there is moderate edema between the iliotibial band and the lateral femoral condyle, compatible with iliotibial band friction syndrome.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Shallow trochlear sulcus. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Findings consistent with iliotibial band friction syndrome.
2. Healed osteochondral lesion at the medial femoral condyle near the intercondylar notch, with overlying cartilage fissuring.
3. Minimal, ruptured Baker cyst.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    assess mpfl tear, osteochondral fragment   .

PRIOR IMAGING:    
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The patella is laterally subluxed and there is diffuse edema seen along the course of the medial patellofemoral ligament consistent with a high-grade injury. This extends to the femoral attachment and also involves the attachment at the patella. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is intraosseous edema within the medial patella and contour flattening of the medial surface of the patella. There is associated edema in the lateral femoral condyle consistent associated with the osteochondral impaction along the lateral cortical surface in keeping with transient lateral dislocation of the patella associated with osteochondral impaction of the medial surface of the patella and lateral femoral condyle.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is trochlea dysplasia and lateralization of the tibial tubercle with the TT-TG distance measuring 2.1 cm. Articular cartilage of the patella demonstrates focal fraying at the patellar apex. The trochlear surface is reasonably well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment appears to be well maintained.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is mild intrinsic signal within the posterior cruciate ligament but intact fibers are present and the signal changes may in part be artifactual.

There is edema around the proximal and mid fibers of the medial collateral ligament consistent with low-grade medial collateral ligament sprain.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon, popliteus tendon and IT band all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small to moderate knee effusion. There is no Baker's cyst demonstrated.

INTERPRETATION: 

Torn medial patellofemoral ligament associated with bone contusions an osteochondral fracturing of the medial surface of patella and lateral femoral condyle associated with transient dislocation of the patellofemoral joint.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Background changes of lateralization of the tibial tubercle and shallowness of the trochlear groove predisposing to patellar dislocation.

Low-grade medial collateral ligament tear.

Nonspecific signal in the posterior cruciate ligament favored to be artifactual.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Rotura meniscal medial izquierdo.
Hallazgos:
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
El menisco lateral es de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Rotura compleja con componente principal horizontal oblicuo del cuerpo y cuerno posterior del
menisco medial con leve extrusión meniscal. Esto se asocia a edema de las partes blandas
regionales.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de distribución difusa del compartimento femorotibial medial
con pequeños focos con cambios óseos secundarios periféricos del cóndilo femoral medial.
Cartílago del compartimento femorotibial lateral con condropatía superficial.
Úlceras condrales de espesor total de la tróclea femoral, predominando su región inferior con
cambios óseos secundarios.
Condropatía rotuliana superficial difusa.
Leve a moderado derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura compleja del menisco medial con extrusión asociada y edema de las partes blandas
adyacentes.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 2 de distribución difusa del compartimento femorotibial medial.
Condropatía lesiones focales grado 4 periférica del cóndilo femoral medial.
Cartílago del compartimento femorotibial lateral y de la rótula con condropatía superficial.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 4 de la tróclea femoral.
Leve a moderado derrame articular

MRI  KNEE  -  RIGHT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Right knee chronic pain, trauma. Some abnormalities on x-ray and ultrasound.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:

Medial meniscus:  Intact.

Medial compartment articular cartilage:  Small focus of mild chondrosis central weightbearing aspect medial tibial plateau.

MCL:  Intact.

Lateral meniscus:  Minimal apical truncation of the lateral meniscal body compatible with a tiny partial nondisplaced radial tear. No meniscal extrusion.

Lateral compartment articular cartilage:  Scattered foci of mild chondrosis.

LCL complex:  Intact.

ACL:  Intact.

PCL:  Intact.

Quadriceps and patellar tendons:  Mild tendinosis involving the medial insertional fibers of the biceps tendon, without tear. Mild proximal patellar tendinosis without tear..

Patellofemoral alignment:  Normal. 

Patellofemoral cartilage:  Extensive fissuring of articular cartilage overlying the patellar articular surface with foci of full-thickness cartilage denuding at the patellar apex and along the lateral patellar facet.

Joint effusion:  Trace joint effusion in the suprapatellar recess. 

Intra-articular bodies:  None.

Bone marrow: As above. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

Popliteal fossa:  No additional abnormality.

Other findings:  None.


INTERPRETATION:
1. Tiny partial nondisplaced radial tear involving the body of the lateral meniscus with lateral meniscal extrusion.
2. Tricompartment chondrosis most pronounced involving the patellofemoral compartment, consistent with moderate patellofemoral predominant osteoarthritis of the right knee.
3. Mild quadriceps tendinosis without tear.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Posterior knee pain, tripped [DATE] on sidewalk
Comparison: Right knee radiographs 11/[DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 3.0 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol. A marker was placed at the site of reported symptoms.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst. Ganglion cyst associated with the popliteus tendon sheath extending into the popliteus muscle.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Thin complete radial tear of the posterior root of the medial meniscus within 1 cm of the attachment. Mild extrusion and displacement into the meniscotibial recess. Mild edema at the meniscocapsular attachment likely reflecting a low-grade strain.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Attenuated consistent with prior sprain.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, presumably related to adjacent meniscal pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Benign-appearing lymph node in the popliteal fossa.

IMPRESSION:
1. Thin complete radial tear of the posterior root of the medial meniscus with mild extrusion and displacement into the meniscotibial recess.

2. Probable associated low-grade meniscocapsular sprain.

3. Attenuated anterior cruciate ligament presumably related to prior sprain.

ADDENDUM:
Moderate trochlear chondrosis with areas of high-grade partial and full-thickness cartilage loss at the central trochlea with subchondral edema.

Zentrierte Stellung im rechten Kniegelenk. Zentrierte Stellung der Patella. Keine trochleäre Dysplasie. Regelrechter Knorpelbelag retropatellar. Gering streifige hypointense Signalveränderungen des Knorpelbelages zentral in der Trochlea mit subchondral kleinzystischen Veränderungen und Ödemsignal, hier V.a. fokal osteochondrale Läsion (5/15, 4/19 + 6/20). Keine wesentliche Chondropathie femoro-tibial im medialen und lateralen Kompartiment oder retropatellar. Keine wesentliche Gelenkspaltverschmälerung. Kleine umschrieben T2-hyperintense Läsion in der Femurmetaphyse mit 7 mm (5/19, 4/14), morph. passend zu einem Enchondrom. Gering Gelenkerguss, keine freienn Gelenkkörper. Intaktes vorderes und hinteres Kreuzband. Intaktes mediales und laterales Kollateralband. Unauffällige Darstellung des medialen und lateralen Meniskus bezogen auf Formgebung und Signalintensität. Intakte Darstellung der Quadriceps- und Patellarsehne. Unauffällige Darstellung der umgebenden Muskulatur und Weichteile.
